title: Answer-vs-Thinking Honesty Gap in Open-Weight Reasoning Models

original_idea.body: Answer-vs-Thinking Honesty Gap. Problem: the prevalence and triggers of think-vs-answer divergence in open-weight reasoning models are under-characterized. Direction: on an open reasoning model with separate think/answer segments, extract the implied answer from the trace vs the final answer, measure disagreement, stratify by difficulty and sycophantic pressure.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: think-vs-answer divergence misleads users and monitors, a concrete faithfulness concern.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Extract implied answer from think + compare to final.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused divergence-rate metric; stratification adds scope.

low_compute.reasoning: Open reasoning model inference, single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: A recent paper studies exactly this divergence on open-weight models; this is close replication.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: A recent paper directly studies think-vs-answer divergence on open-weight models; this is largely a replication.
